valuation_philosophy: FIG is a recent IPO (listed NYSE July 31, 2025), with under 12 months of public trading history. There is essentially no multi-year public market trading record from which to anchor EV/Revenue or EV/FCF multiples historically. The DCF is therefore anchored to fundamentals — adjusted FCF and revenue growth — rather than mean-reversion to a historical trading range. Peer SaaS comparables (companies growing 30-45% with improving FCF margins) trading at 8-15x NTM revenue are used as a cross-check only. GAAP metrics are distorted by $1.364B of IPO-triggered SBC in FY2025; all projections use adjusted/non-GAAP FCF as the cash-flow basis.

inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 Adjusted FCF (non-GAAP, excludes SBC-related cash taxes)

historical_growth.eps_note: GAAP EPS is deeply negative due to IPO-triggered SBC events ($858M Q2 2024, $1.14B Q3 2025). Not meaningful as a growth metric.
historical_growth.equity_note: Book value swings are driven by IPO mechanics, convertible preferred conversions, and lumpy SBC charges — not underlying business growth. Not used as a growth anchor.
historical_growth.fcf_note: FY2023 adj FCF $91.8M (18.2% margin) → FY2024 $181.3M (24.2% margin) → FY2025 $246.2M (23.3% margin). Q1 2026 adj FCF $89.5M (26.8% margin), signaling FY2026 margin recovery. 2-yr CAGR boosted by margin expansion from a low FY2023 base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and EPS growth rates are not meaningful for Figma due to IPO mechanics, dual-trigger RSU SBC events ($858M Q2 2024, $1.14B Q3 2025), and convertible preferred conversions. Revenue CAGR (44.6% 2-yr) and adjusted FCF CAGR (63.8% 2-yr, margin-expansion-driven) are the relevant anchors. Growth is moderated: FY2026 guidance implies ~35% revenue growth; Q1 2026 actual +46% YoY indicates re-acceleration. Base case Y1 growth set at 35% in line with guidance midpoint.

base.rationale: Revenue decelerates from FY2026 guidance of ~35% toward mature SaaS levels (~16%) over five years. FCF margins expand from FY2025's 23.3% toward 33% as AI credit revenue scales, SBC normalizes post-IPO, and operational leverage improves. WACC of 10.5% reflects high-growth SaaS risk profile, recent IPO uncertainty, and moderate beta.

bull.rationale: AI credit monetization and Figma Make drive re-acceleration beyond guidance. NDR sustains 135-145% range. Code Layers (July 2026) catalyzes developer seat upgrades. International monetization gap closes faster. FCF margins reach 40% in Y5 as AI revenue scales with near-zero marginal cost per seat. Lower WACC reflects proven execution and durable competitive position.

bear.rationale: AI-native competitors (Cursor, v0, GitHub Copilot) erode design-phase relevance. August 2026 lockup expiry triggers sustained selling pressure. Gross margin compression from AI inference costs persists. Enterprise deal cycles lengthen in a macro slowdown. SBC remains elevated, suppressing true FCF. Higher WACC reflects execution risk and lockup/dilution overhang.

sensitivity.note: Base case FCF profile (growth rates and margins). Rows = WACC, Cols = Terminal Growth Rate.

sanity_check.thin_history_caveat: FIG has been publicly traded since July 31, 2025 — under 12 months. There is essentially no multi-year public trading history to anchor EV/Revenue or EV/FCF multiples. The figures below are point-in-time observations only, not a statistically meaningful historical range.

market_implied_multiples.note: At $18.62, the market prices FIG at ~5.7x FY2026E revenue — below the typical 8-15x range for SaaS companies growing 30-45%. This reflects: (a) post-IPO hype unwind (-87% from $142 ATH), (b) August 2026 lockup overhang, (c) AI disruption discount, (d) GAAP profitability concerns.

base_iv_implied_multiples.note: Base IV of $24.88 implies ~8.0x FY2026E EV/Revenue — within the lower bound of the 8-15x peer range for 35% growth SaaS. This is not unreasonable on a fundamentals basis, though elevated relative to current market sentiment.

sbc_warning.note: GAAP SBC of $1.364B in FY2025 (129% of revenue) is structurally distorting. The bulk ($975.7M) was a one-time IPO-triggered dual-trigger RSU event. Ongoing SBC from post-IPO grants (29M+ new RSUs to leadership) remains substantial — estimated $200-350M/yr going forward. Adjusted FCF excludes cash taxes on SBC exercises; the true economic cost of SBC is real and ongoing.

lockup_overhang_warning.note: Extended lockup covering approximately 54.1% of outstanding shares (~283M shares) expires August 31, 2026. This is a material supply/valuation overhang. Even if only a fraction of insiders sell at expiry, the potential supply exceeds typical daily trading volumes by many multiples. The bear case specifically incorporates this risk through a higher WACC (12%) and lower growth assumptions.

sanity_check.sensitivity_notable: At WACC 12.5% and terminal growth 2.0%, the sensitivity matrix produces an intrinsic value of exactly $18.62 — the current market price. This means the market is pricing FIG as if it will face the highest cost of capital in the sensitivity range AND the lowest terminal growth rate. This is either deeply pessimistic or accurately reflects execution/disruption risk.

warning_banners.title: AI Disruption Risk
warning_banners.message: Code-generation tools (Cursor, v0, GitHub Copilot) may reduce demand for the design phase. Figma's response (Code Layers, Figma Make) is promising but unproven at scale. Bear case reflects a scenario where this risk materialises.
